metadata.title: kikx
metadata.description: Build real, editable infrastructure files in your browser: Ansible, Kubernetes and Terraform you own.

header.github: {repository} on GitHub, {stars, plural, one {# star} other {# stars}}, {forks, plural, one {# fork} other {# forks}}

home.intro: Render real, editable infrastructure files straight into your project: Ansible inventories, group vars and playbooks, Kubernetes manifests and Terraform. No hidden dependency, just <accent>plain files</accent> you own.

resume.kept: {count, plural, one {# component} other {# components}} and any unsaved drafts are kept in this browser.
resume.confirmBody: Its {count, plural, one {# component} other {# components}} and unsaved drafts are removed from this browser.

cli.title: Prefer the terminal?
cli.hint: the same steps with the kikx CLI

build.title: Blank project
build.body: Fill in your project's details, add the components you need, and download the result. Nothing is read from or written to your machine until you hit download.

preset.body: Continue from a .kikx-preset.json you downloaded earlier.

home.dataFlowLink: See how data flows through kikx

templates.title: Start from a template
templates.body: A complete, editable project to adapt instead of starting from an empty page.

welcome.title: Welcome to kikx
welcome.description: kikx renders real infrastructure files for Ansible, Kubernetes and Terraform that you own and edit like any other code. This tour takes a minute.

cli.title: Prefer the terminal?
cli.description: Everything here is also in the kikx CLI. Open this to see the commands you would run.

templates.title: Start from a template
templates.description: Open a complete project, from a single server to a kubeadm cluster or a multi-tier platform, and adapt it.

new-project.title: Or start from a blank project
new-project.description: Name the project, pick a namespace and an output folder, then add components one by one.

open-preset.title: Pick up where you left off
open-preset.description: Every project downloads as a preset file. Open it here to keep editing.

data-flow.title: How it fits together
data-flow.description: A diagram of how the dashboard, the CLI and the API turn a template into files.

tour-button.title: Replay this tour
tour-button.description: Open it again from here on any page with a tour, including the builder.

catalog.title: Components, stage by stage
catalog.description: Provision servers, list them in an inventory, configure them with playbooks and roles, then deploy to Kubernetes. A tick shows each stage you have covered.

editor.title: Fill in, watch it render
editor.description: Every field has a sensible default. The files below update as you type; press ⌘/Ctrl + Enter to add the component.

project.title: Your project
project.description: Everything you have added, with its files. Click one to edit it, or download the whole project as a preset to reopen later.

views.title: Architecture and checks
views.description: Architecture draws how your components connect. Checks catches conflicts such as duplicate hosts, missing groups and unknown roles before you ship.

download.title: Take the files
download.description: Download everything as a .zip of plain files. Nothing touches your machine until you do.

phone.title: Do you really want to do this on your phone?
phone.body: You think you're doing great, but trust me: get up and grab your computer. I was too lazy to do it too.
phone.copyLink: Copy the link for my computer
phone.copied: Link copied. Open it on your computer.
phone.copyFailed: Couldn't copy the link. Copy it from the address bar instead.

builder.goBack: Go back and fill them in

header.homeHint: Back to the home page. Your project stays saved in this browser.

builder.scaffolded: Scaffolded {count, plural, one {# role} other {# roles}}
builder.scaffoldedDetail: Empty tasks, defaults, handlers and meta. Open one to see its files.

provision.hint: Optional. Skip it if the servers already exist.

inventory.label: Inventory
inventory.hint: List the servers and sort them into groups.

configure.label: Configure
configure.hint: Decide which roles run on which groups.

deploy.label: Deploy
deploy.hint: Kubernetes manifests for what runs on the cluster.

custom.label: From registry URL

toasts.files: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} in the project.

saveBar.draftKept: Draft kept in this browser · ⌘/Ctrl + Enter to save

preview.waiting: The preview appears as soon as the required fields are filled in.
preview.invalid: Some fields are incomplete. Showing the last valid render.

fields.name: Name

nameHelp.role: Writes {path}. Use this name in a playbook.
nameHelp.k8s: Also the default app label, so a Deployment and Service with the same name find each other.

fields.providerHelp: Every Terraform item in the registry is listed here. For another provider, load its registry item from Custom.

inventory.hostsBody: One row per server. Put it in every group it belongs to: kikx writes its address once and references it by name elsewhere.
inventory.imported: Imported {hosts, plural, one {# host} other {# hosts}} and {groups, plural, one {# group} other {# groups}}
inventory.groupsBody: Nest groups (:children) and give them shared vars (:vars). Groups your hosts use exist already, so add a row only to nest them or attach vars.

host.inheritNote: Leave user and port empty to inherit them from a group's vars. Setting them here overrides the group.

import.title: Import an existing inventory
import.body: Paste an INI inventory (or pick the file). Hosts listed in several groups are merged into one host with several groups; group :children and :vars come along too.
import.counts: {hosts, plural, one {# host} other {# hosts}} · {groups, plural, one {# group} other {# groups}}

warnings.outside: Line {line}: "{text}" is outside any [group] section, so it was skipped.
warnings.conflict: {host}: {field} is "{existing}" in one group but "{value}" in [{group}]. Kept the first.
warnings.noAddress: {host} has no ansible_host. Ansible will try to resolve the name itself.

groupVars.noInventory: Add an Inventory to pick from its groups.
groupVars.yamlHelp: Paste lists, maps, anything YAML: it's written as-is. Ideal for copying an existing group_vars file.
groupVars.nested: This YAML has nested values. Keep editing it as YAML so nothing is lost.

plays.title: Plays
plays.body: Each play runs its roles, in order, on one inventory group. Most playbooks need one; add more to run different roles on different groups from the same file.
plays.heading: Play {number}
plays.name: Name
plays.roles: Roles, in the order they run

conditions.title: Role conditions (when:)
conditions.placeholder: always runs, or a Jinja condition

tasks.title: Pre-tasks & post-tasks
tasks.help: A YAML list of tasks, written as-is under pre_tasks: / post_tasks:.

site.title: Imports, in run order
site.body: ansible-playbook site.yml runs these top to bottom. Pick playbooks from this project, or type the path of one that already lives in your repo.

custom.title: Custom component
custom.body: Point at any registry-item.json (a URL or a local path) and render it. No kikx update required.
custom.placeholder: URL or path to a registry-item.json
custom.name: Name
custom.replaced: Replaced {count, plural, one {# component} other {# components}}
custom.added: Added {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}

conflicts.title: {count, plural, one {This file already exists} other {# files already exist}}
conflicts.body: A project can only have one writer per file. Replacing removes the component that currently owns {count, plural, one {it} other {them}}. Expand a file to compare.
conflicts.collateral: Also removed with {count, plural, one {that component} other {those components}}: <files></files>

project.title: Project
project.summary: {components, plural, one {# component} other {# components}} · {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} in {dir}
project.empty: Nothing yet. Most projects start with an Inventory.
project.viewing: Rendered by {component}. Edit the component to change it.

setup.explain: setup bootstraps a new kikx project from this file. apply vendors it into a project you already have, with no kikx.toml and no backend required.

checks.empty: Add components and kikx will check how they fit together.
checks.clear: No conflicts found. Hosts, groups, playbooks and manifests all line up.
checks.intro: kikx cross-checks components against each other: duplicate files, hosts with two addresses, host vars that silently override group vars, plays aimed at groups that don't exist, and more. Errors break the output; warnings are likely mistakes; notes are just good to know.
checks.scaffold: Scaffold {count, plural, one {# role} other {# roles}}

dupFile.title: {count} components write {file}
dupFile.detail: Only the last one survives in the download. Remove or rename one of them.

cycle.title: Group nesting loops: {path}
cycle.detail: Ansible refuses to load an inventory whose :children form a cycle.

emptyChild.title: [{group}:children] lists "{child}", which has no hosts
emptyChild.detail: Probably a typo, or add hosts to that group.

address.title: {host} has two addresses: {first} and {second}
address.detail: The same host name points at different machines. Ansible uses whichever it reads last.

override.title: {host} sets {key}={value}, overriding [{group}:vars] {key}={groupValue}
override.detail: Host vars win over group vars. Clear {key} on the host if the group value is the one you want.

multiInventory.title: {count} inventories in this project
multiInventory.detail: Fine for separate environments; pass the right one with -i. Checks treat their groups as one pool.

layouts.title: Group "{group}" has both group_vars/{group}.yml and group_vars/{group}/main.yml
layouts.detail: Ansible loads and merges both, so a key set twice depends on load order. Keep one layout.

unknownGroup.title: group_vars/{group}.yml targets a group no inventory defines
unknownGroup.detail: Those variables will never be loaded. Check the spelling against your inventory groups.

shadow.title: {key} is set in both [{group}:vars] and group_vars/{group}.yml
shadow.detail: group_vars/{group}.yml wins. Keep it in one place.
shadow.detailValues: group_vars/{group}.yml wins ({fileValue} over {value}). Keep it in one place.

playHosts.title: Play "{play}" targets "{target}", which isn't in the inventory
playHosts.detail: The play will match no hosts and silently do nothing.

externalRoles.title: {playbook} uses {count, plural, one {# role} other {# roles}} kikx doesn't vendor
externalRoles.detail: {roles}: they must already exist under roles/ in your repo, or scaffold empty ones here.

siteMissing.title: {site}.yml imports {path}, which this project doesn't produce
siteMissing.detail: Fine if the file already exists in your repo; otherwise add that playbook.

notImported.title: {path} isn't imported by any site playbook
notImported.detail: It only runs if you call it directly.

serviceSelector.title: Service {service} selects app={selector}, but no deployment has that label
serviceSelector.detail: Its endpoints will be empty. Name the deployment the same, or set the app label.

ingressBackend.title: Ingress {ingress} routes to service "{backend}", which isn't in the project

diagram.empty: Add a component to see the architecture start forming.
diagram.hint: Laid out left to right in the order things happen. Hover a node to trace its connections, click it to edit. Export to draw.io to keep refining the diagram by hand.

nodes.children: {count, plural, one {# child group} other {# child groups}}
nodes.plays: {plays, plural, one {# play} other {# plays}} · {roles, plural, one {# role} other {# roles}}
nodes.role: Ansible role · {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}

flow.title: Data flow
flow.body: Pick how you'd drive kikx: the path it actually takes lights up.

notFound.title: This route hasn't been <accent>vendored</accent>
notFound.body: There's no page here. While you find your way back, here's a dad joke:
notFound.jokeFailed: Couldn't even fetch a joke. That's a 404 on a 404.

validation.portWhole: Port must be a whole number
validation.groupNameFormat: Letters, digits, _ and - only; start with a letter or _
validation.addressInvalid: Enter a valid IP address or hostname
validation.hostGroupsRequired: Put the host in at least one group
validation.hostDuplicate: "{name}" is already host #{index}. Add the extra groups to that host instead
validation.playHosts: Pick a group to run on
validation.folderRelative: Use a relative folder like playbooks

errors.notConfigured: NEXT_PUBLIC_KIKX_API_URL is not set. Point it at your kikx backend (see web/.env.example).
errors.network: Can't reach the kikx backend. Check that it's running and that NEXT_PUBLIC_KIKX_API_URL points at it.
errors.notPreset: That isn't a kikx preset: it has no components list.
errors.presetComponent: Component #{index} is missing a reference or name.
